calls.head: Lankinen isn’t cursed against the Oilers
calls.body: Lankinen has been shaky against the Oilers since 2023-24, well below his usual. It looks like a pattern, but across three seasons a goalie’s record against one team told us nothing about the next meeting. Expect the usual Lankinen.
calls.call: If Lankinen starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .894 than to his .855 against the Oilers.
calls.nums: 6 starts against Edmonton: .855 save percentage · .894 against everyone else
calls.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 6 against Edmonton, 3,059 shots against everyone else
calls.happened: He didn’t start, so this call can’t be judged.

calls.head: Special teams lean toward the Oilers
calls.body: The Oilers’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Canucks’ kill is near the bottom of the league. The Canucks need to stay out of the box.
calls.call: The Oilers’ power play creates at least their usual 9.6 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: Edmonton 1st for power play (9.6 expected goals per 60) · Vancouver 27th for penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: Edmonton’s power play created 11.0 expected goals per 60 in 6:48 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 9.6, and scored 2 goals.

calls.head: The Oilers should get some good looks
calls.body: The Canucks have struggled to prevent dangerous shots, and the Oilers don’t waste many.
calls.call: The Oilers’ average shot has at least their usual 6.5% chance of going in.
calls.nums: Edmonton 8th for shot quality (a 6.5% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Vancouver 31st for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: Edmonton’s average shot had a 5.7% chance of going in, against their usual 6.5%.

calls.head: The Oilers’ defense joins the attack; the Canucks’ stays home
calls.body: On shots from defensemen, Edmonton is one of the league’s best and Vancouver is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Oilers’ defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Canucks’.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On share of 5-on-5 shot attempts taken by defensemen, Edmonton had 39% and Vancouver 26%. Coming in, Edmonton was at 37% and Vancouver at 31%.

VAN.head: We gave Vancouver only a 27% chance, and it went the way we feared.

EDM.head: We gave Edmonton a 73% chance, and Edmonton delivered.

surprises.head: A rough night for D. Levi
surprises.body: D. Levi allowed 7 goals on shots worth 2.8 expected goals, 4.2 more than expected. Starting goalies had a night this rough about once every 200 starts over the last three seasons.

surprises.head: Vancouver got the good looks
surprises.body: Vancouver’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: a 10.1% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.0% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 175 games.

surprises.head: Edmonton tried a different line
surprises.body: C. McDavid, L. Draisaitl, V. Podkolzin played 12:01 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Edmonton’s usual lines.

story.head: The Oilers beat the Canucks
paras: The Oilers had this one put away early. Vasily Podkolzin opened the scoring midway through the first. Leon Draisaitl added two goals. Eight different Oilers scored. Kasperi Kapanen scored the winner midway through the second.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. By our Swing measure, Connor McDavid had the best night of anyone. The Oilers tried a line they hadn’t used before: McDavid, Draisaitl and Podkolzin, and it had a hand in five of their goals.

items.text: Whether the Oilers keep that line together at home against Seattle on Saturday.
Two of the preview’s three calls held.
